annotation.title_clean: Enrolled Senate Bill No. 1541 (Oklahoma): Operation of Fully Autonomous Vehicles
annotation.title_en: Enrolled Senate Bill No. 1541 (Oklahoma): Operation of Fully Autonomous Vehicles
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Oklahoma Legislature (Sen. Rosino and Rep. Bergstrom)
annotation.summary_en: Oklahoma enrolled act allowing fully autonomous (SAE level 4-5) vehicles to operate without a human driver, requiring a law enforcement interaction plan, $1 million insurance, accident reporting, registration and titling, and treating the automated driving system as licensed driver, with state preemption of local regulation. Effective November 1, 2022.
key_provisions_or_claims: Fully autonomous vehicles may operate without a human driver if they can achieve a minimal risk condition on system failure and comply with traffic laws.
Operators must submit a law enforcement interaction plan to the Department of Public Safety.
Proof of financial responsibility of at least $1,000,000 is required.
Automated driving system is deemed the driver and licensed operator when engaged.
State exclusively governs AVs and preempts county and municipal regulation.
